reason: Introduce independent decision/evidence tests and enforce exact-run quality admission, source-bound policy reasoning, reproducible scheduled exploration, retained measurements and read-only health monitoring, as requested by the repository owner.
risk: The new required check may block merges for real regressions or unavailable scanner setup. Infrastructure failures remain explicit. Trend calibration starts with real hosted measurements; fixed limits and reviewed mutation equivalence are not automatically relaxed.
validation: Local full backend gate after the evidence-copy optimization: 1785 passed, eight optional checks skipped; types and all eight critical coverage floors passed. 57 focused governance/selection cases and 38 storage/property cases passed. Four demonstrated negative controls cover policy review and import trend warnings. Local 10000-entry and 13000-revision workloads pass; the hosted import/history recheck passed at 57.7 seconds against the unchanged 60-second import limit. All hosted checks must verify the final candidate; CodeQL is currently blocked by the private repository configuration.
coverage_impact: Replace three self-comparison validator properties with independent positive/negative expectations and focused evidence mutations. Retire only the obsolete mutmut shell-command assertion. Add decision, stateful, recovery and history coverage; preserve existing UI, package and release checks. Governance test fixtures contain skip markers solely to test scope review. New public decision functions and modules require an explicit coverage decision. Preserve failing Playwright traces and maintenance browser artifacts so a first-attempt failure remains diagnosable without a retry. The first hosted import budget failure is addressed by removing redundant evidence copies while retaining storage versions, hashes, transaction boundaries and deep isolation. 38 storage/property cases and the unchanged local 10000-entry budget pass; hosted validation must rerun. Import warning baselines distinguish workload sizes and expose near-budget and sustained regressions before hard failure.
